card.title: EXPEDITIONARY CORPS
card.flavorText: The French Expeditionary Corps, also known as the French Expeditionary Corps in Italy, was a force of 112,000 Free French soldiers, 60% were Maghrebis (mostly Morroccan) and 40% Pied-Noirs (people of French and other European origin, born in Algeria under French rule). The corps fought with the U.S. Fifth Army in the Italian Campaign during WWII under the command of Général de Corps d'Armée Alphonse Juin. The FEC fought in the First Battle of Monte Cassino in January 1944. In May 1944 the FEC fought in the battle for the Gustav Line, which it managed to penetrate in less than two days of fighting and thrust forward in what is considered one of the most brilliant and daring advances of the war in Italy. After the Italian Campaign the soldiers were withdrawn to Africa where they joined France’s 1st Army which landed in southern France after Operation Dragoon.
